title: THE LESSON I LEARNED FROM THE BROKEN TABLETS
paragraphs: THE LESSON I LEARNED FROM THE BROKEN TABLETS
There are moments in life when everything you believed was finally coming together suddenly shatters in your hands.

You spend years praying, sacrificing, obeying, waiting for God to move. Then one phone call, one betrayal, one bad decision, one moment of weakness, and suddenly you find yourself standing in the middle of pieces you cannot put back together.
Most people know the story of Moses receiving the Ten Commandments.
Far fewer understand the devastating lesson hidden inside the broken tablets.
And perhaps even fewer realize that the story is really about us.
It is the story of every person who has watched something sacred collapse.
It is the story of scandal.
But even more importantly, it is the story of grace.
Because from the very beginning, God was already writing a redemption story.
After God delivered Israel from slavery in Egypt, Moses ascended Mount Sinai to receive God's covenant. There, God Himself inscribed His law upon two stone tablets.
"And He gave unto Moses, when He had made an end of communing with him upon mount Sinai, two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God."
The Hebrew phrase is especially striking:

"לֻחֹת אֶבֶן כְּתֻבִים בְּאֶצְבַּע אֱלֹהִים"
(Luchot Even Ketuvim Be'etzba Elohim)
"Tablets of stone written by the finger of God."
The tablets represented something far greater than commandments.
God was not merely giving rules.
Yet while Moses was receiving the covenant on the mountain, Israel was breaking it below.
Impatient and fearful, they fashioned a golden calf and declared:
The people who had witnessed miracles were already replacing the God who rescued them.
And before we judge them too quickly, we should ask ourselves an uncomfortable question.
How often have we done the same?
We may not bow before golden statues.
Anything we elevate above Christ becomes a modern golden calf.
The tragedy of Exodus is not merely ancient history.
When Moses descended and witnessed the rebellion, Scripture records one of the most dramatic moments in the entire Bible.
"And he cast the tables out of his hands, and brake them beneath the mount."
But what if the broken tablets reveal something profound about the human condition?
The tablets represented God's perfect standard.
Their destruction symbolized humanity's inability to uphold that standard.
The covenant was broken almost immediately.
The Apostle Paul would later write in Romans 3:23:
Sometimes so badly that the pieces seem impossible to recover.
Some of you know exactly what that feels like.
Perhaps your broken tablets have names.
A scandal nobody knows about except you and God.
You look at the shattered pieces and wonder if God can still use your life.
But here is where the story takes a breathtaking turn.
Because God was not finished writing.
Exodus 34 begins with an astonishing command.
"Cut two tablets of stone like the first ones."
God did not abandon His people.
God did not destroy the covenant entirely.
But because God provides a way forward after failure.
Then comes one of the most beautiful self-descriptions God ever gives in Scripture.

"יְהוָה יְהוָה אֵל רַחוּם וְחַנּוּן"
(YHWH YHWH El Rachum Ve'Chanun)
"The LORD, the LORD God, merciful and gracious."
The Hebrew word רַחוּם (rachum) speaks of deep compassion.
The word חַנּוּן (chanun) means gracious, favor-giving, undeserved kindness.
This is who God reveals Himself to be immediately after one of Israel's greatest failures.
The broken tablets reveal a truth many Christians spend years trying to understand.
Failure is not the end of the story when Jesus is the author.
The Bible is filled with broken people.
The Samaritan woman carried a history she could not escape.
Yet God transformed every one of their stories.
Because grace is greater than failure.
This reaches its ultimate fulfillment in Jesus Christ.
The Law engraved on stone exposed humanity's inability to save itself.
But Christ came to accomplish what broken sinners never could.
"For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ."
The Greek word for grace is:
At the cross, Jesus took every shattered piece of human rebellion upon Himself.
The greatest miracle of the Gospel is not that Jesus makes good people better.
It is that He redeems broken people completely.
Many believers spend years trying to hide their broken tablets.
God often uses them as testimony.
The scars become evidence of grace.
The failure becomes part of the witness.
That is why our theme remains eternally true:
Maybe you are reading this while staring at broken pieces.
Maybe your life looks nothing like what you imagined.
Maybe shame has become your constant companion.
The broken tablets were not the end.
And neither are your broken places.
The God who rewrote Israel's story still rewrites stories today.
The cross stands as eternal proof.
Jesus specializes in restoring what sin destroys.
And sometimes He creates something even more beautiful than what existed before.
Because redemption does not merely repair.
If this message touched something deep inside you, do not keep it to yourself.
What broken tablet has God been helping you surrender?
Your testimony may become the encouragement someone else desperately needs today.
Those who desire to glorify God through supporting Gospel-centered ministry can join our growing community of believers committed to advancing the message of Jesus Christ.
One day you will realize the thing you thought disqualified you became the very place where God's grace became undeniable.
